questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A defendant has been charged with making a false statement to a federally insured financial institution to secure a loan. At trial, the prosecutor calls the defendant's wife as a willing witness to testify that the defendant told her in confidence that he had misrepresented his assets on the loan application.
The defendant objects to his wife's testimony. Should the testimony be admitted?

choices.A: No, because even though the wife is a willing witness, the defendant has the right to exclude confidential marital communications in federal court.
choices.B: No, but only if the law of the state where the defendant and his wife reside recognizes a privilege for confidential marital communications.
choices.C: Yes, because in federal court the right not to testify belongs to the testifying spouse, and she is a willing witness.
choices.D: Yes, because while the adverse testimonial privilege is recognized in federal court, the marital communications privilege is not.

questions.explanation:
Spousal privileges
Purpose Privilege holder Duration
Spousal-immunity Shields witness-spouse from testifying against spouse in criminal case about matters that occurred before or during marriage Witness-spouse Only during active marriage
Marital-communications Protects against disclosure of confidential spousal communications made during marriage in criminal & civil cases Both spouses Continues after divorce

In federal court, claims of privilege are generally governed by the common law. Two common law privileges apply to spousal testimony:

  • Spousal-immunity (ie, adverse-testimony) privilege – allows a person to refuse to testify against his/her spouse in a criminal case about any matter that occurred before or during marriage
  • Marital-communications privilege – protects confidential communications between spouses during the marriage from disclosure, discovery, or admission in criminal and civil cases (Choice D)

The spousal-immunity privilege belongs only to the witness-spouse, who can choose to waive the privilege and testify against the defendant-spouse (as seen here). But the marital-communications privilege belongs to both spouses, so one spouse can prevent the other from disclosing a confidential communication. Therefore, the wife's testimony about confidential marital communications should be excluded on this basis (Choice C).

(Choice B) Federal common law privileges apply in federal cases except (1) when the Constitution, a federal statute, or a Supreme Court rule provides otherwise or (2) in diversity cases, where the rules of the state where the court (not the parties) sits will apply. Neither exception applies to this federal criminal case.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the spousal-immunity (ie, adverse-testimony) privilege, a witness-spouse can refuse to testify against his/her spouse in a criminal case about any matter. Under the marital-communications privilege, both spouses can protect confidential communications during marriage from disclosure, discovery, or admission in all cases.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (privilege in general).

被告反对其妻子的证词。该证词是否应被采纳？

zh-choices.A: 不应采纳，因为即使妻子是自愿作证的证人，被告在联邦法院仍有权排除保密的婚姻内交流。
zh-choices.B: 不应采纳，但前提是被告及其妻子居住州的法律承认保密的婚姻内交流特免权。
zh-choices.C: 应采纳，因为在联邦法院，不作证的权利属于作证配偶，而她是自愿作证的证人。
zh-choices.D: 应采纳，因为虽然联邦法院承认配偶不利证言特免权，但不承认婚姻内交流特免权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：丈夫对妻子说过的保密婚内沟通，能不能被妻子自愿作证带进法庭。

三秒认题路径：

婚内密语 → 自愿作证 → 谁能挡 → 选排除

核心法律规则

联邦法院里，特权通常适用普通法。这里要先分清两种 配偶特权（spousal privileges）：配偶免证特权（spousal immunity / adverse-testimony privilege） 只让作证的配偶自己决定要不要拒证，考场意思：这是 witness-spouse 的按钮。

但 婚内通信特权（marital-communications privilege） 保护的是婚姻存续期间的保密交流，考场意思：只要内容是秘密说的，另一方就能把它挡在法庭外，而且这项特权不因离婚就消失。

所以这题里，妻子愿意作证，不代表丈夫就失去阻止她披露 confidential marital communication 的权利。

核心判例： Fed. R. Evid. 501 及普通法配偶特权规则锁定本题：妻子能自愿出庭，但丈夫仍可用婚内通信特权排除保密内容。

思维导图

先看：证据是“配偶自愿作证”还是“保密婚内通信”？
YES 自愿作证：先别急着放行，继续问是谁在主张哪一种特权。
配偶免证特权（spousal immunity）只归作证配偶；她愿意说，就不能靠它拦住。
→ 这个门过了，不等于所有配偶相关证据都能进。
NO / 另一路：如果是婚内秘密沟通，直接转看婚内通信特权。
婚内通信特权（marital-communications privilege）归双方；一方反对，就能挡住保密内容。
→ 结论：妻子可上庭，但那句“我丈夫私下告诉我他造假”应被排除。
最终答案：选 A，排除保密婚内通信，而不是只看她愿不愿意说。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然妻子是 willing witness，那她说什么都能进。

但考试真正问的是：谁有权挡住这段 confidential marital communication，不是她本人想不想说。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干抓到的是 confidential marital communication，这类内容在联邦普通法下可由任一配偶阻止披露，所以妻子愿意作证也不能放行。

❌ 法律适用 | 适用法域误判

✕ B: 把联邦刑事案硬拽去套 state law，法源就错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权主体误判

✕ C: 只盯着 witness-spouse，忘了这里挡的是婚内通信。

❌ 事实误判 | 把两种特权拆错

✕ D: 把 adverse-testimony 和婚内通信特权分家太死，结论就反了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分“谁能拒证”，再分“谁能挡内容”；看到保密婚内谈话，优先想婚内通信特权。

考场速记

记忆口诀：配偶免证特权（spousal immunity） 看“谁上不上证人席”，婚内通信特权（marital-communications privilege） 看“这句话能不能说出来”。

一句话带走：妻子愿意说，不等于丈夫不能拦住保密婚内通信。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A plaintiff, the owner of a motel chain, brought a breach-of-contract action against a defendant, a construction company, in federal court. The plaintiff alleged that the defendant's poor workmanship in constructing the plaintiff's new motel led to major defects in the motel's foundation. The plaintiff further alleged that the defendant knew about the defects but willfully concealed them.
During settlement negotiations, the defendant produced a quality control report that it had created during the motel's construction but had not previously shared with the plaintiff. The report indicated that the defendant was aware of the foundation defects, and it included an estimate on the cost of repair. The defendant relied on the report during the settlement negotiations in order to justify its settlement offer; however, no settlement was reached.
At trial, the plaintiff seeks to introduce the quality control report to establish the issue of willful concealment.
Is the report admissible?

choices.A: No, because all statements made during settlement negotiations are inadmissible.
choices.B: No, because the report is hearsay not within any exception.
choices.C: Yes, because statements made in settlement negotiations are admissible when offered to prove the validity of a claim.
choices.D: Yes, because the report was created for purposes other than settlement negotiations and is otherwise admissible.

questions.explanation:
Compromise offers & negotiations
(FRE 408)
Applicability
  • Offers made with intent to compromise (ie, avoid or end) claim
  • Conduct/statements made during compromise negotiations about claim
Prohibited use Not admissible to:
  • prove/disprove validity or amount of disputed claim or
  • impeach by prior inconsistent statement or contradiction
Exceptions Conduct/statements admissible for above purposes if:
  • made during negotiations in civil dispute involving government regulatory, investigative, or enforcement agency and offered in subsequent criminal case
Admissible for other purpose—eg:
  • proving witness's bias or prejudice
  • negating contention of undue delay
  • proving effort to obstruct criminal investigation or prosecution

FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence.

Federal Rule of Evidence (FRE) 408 is an exclusionary rule designed to encourage compromise and settlement of disputes. As a result, the following evidence is generally not admissible to prove/disprove the validity or amount of a disputed claim or to impeach a witness with a prior inconsistent statement:

  • Offers of compromise made with the intent to avoid or settle the claim
  • Conduct or statements made during compromise or settlement negotiations

However, FRE 408 does not apply to evidence created for reasons other than settlement, so a party cannot immunize evidence from admission merely by producing it during settlement negotiations (Choice A). Accordingly, evidence created for nonsettlement reasons is admissible so long as it is not barred by another rule (eg, the rule against hearsay). Here, the quality control report was created during the motel's construction and before settlement negotiations were ever contemplated. Therefore, the report is not barred under FRE 408.†

Nor is the report barred by the rule against hearsay, under which out-of-court statements are not admissible to prove the truth of the matter asserted therein. That is because out-of-court statements that are made by a party-opponent对方当事人陈述（非传闻，可直接采纳） (eg, the defendant's report) and offered against that party are excluded from this rule and considered nonhearsay (Choice B). Since there is no other basis for exclusion, the report is admissible.

†In contrast, a similar report made for settlement negotiations would be subject to the limitations set forth in FRE 408.

(Choice C) Statements made during settlement negotiations are not always admissible to prove a claim's validity. Such statements are inadmissible for this purpose unless (1) made during negotiations in a civil dispute involving a government regulatory, investigative, or enforcement agency and (2) offered in a subsequent criminal case.

📌 Educational Objective

Statements made during settlement negotiations are generally inadmissible to prove/disprove the validity of a claim or impeach a party with a prior inconsistent statement. But a party cannot immunize evidence created for reasons other than settlement from admission merely by producing the evidence during settlement negotiations.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 408 (compromise offers and negotiations).

原告是一家连锁汽车旅馆的所有人，在联邦法院对被告（一家建筑公司）提起了违约诉讼。原告指控，被告在建造原告的新汽车旅馆时工艺低劣，导致旅馆地基出现重大缺陷。原告进一步指控，被告明知这些缺陷却故意隐瞒。

在和解谈判期间，被告出示了一份其在汽车旅馆建造期间制作、但此前未与原告分享的质量控制报告。该报告表明被告意识到了地基缺陷，并包含了维修费用的估算。被告在和解谈判中依赖该报告为其和解要约提供理由；然而，双方并未达成和解。

在审判中，原告试图引入该质量控制报告，以证明故意隐瞒的问题。

该报告是否可采纳？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为在和解谈判期间所作的所有陈述都是不可采纳的。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该报告是传闻证据，且不属于任何例外情况。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为在和解谈判中所作的陈述，若用于证明一项主张的有效性，则是可采纳的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该报告是为和解谈判以外的目的而创建的，且在其他方面是可采纳的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Public policy exclusions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：和解谈判规则（FRE 408）只挡“为和解而生”的材料，不会把本来就为施工质控做出来的报告，因后来在谈判中被拿出来用，就一并变成不可采。

三秒认题路径：

先看材料来源 → 再看是否为和解而生 → 再查是否另有排除 → 结论：可采

核心法律规则

一眼抓住规则

和解磋商（compromise negotiations）中的让步、陈述，通常不能拿来证明争议主张的对错或金额，这就是 FRE 408 的考场意思：别用“谈判里说过什么”去证明谁对谁错。

但 FRE 408 只管“为和解而作的东西”或“和解谈判中的话”，不把原本为别的目的做出来的材料，变成特权文件；所以先问这份报告是不是本来就为了 settlement 才写的。

如果材料本来就不是为了和解，而是施工过程中的 质量控制报告（quality control report），那它不被 408 挡住；接着再查别的规则，比如 传闻规则（hearsay），若是对方当事人自己的陈述，就常常能进来。

核心判例：本题不靠单独判例卡死，而是直接套 FRE 408：后来在和解里拿出来，并不会把“事前为施工所作”的报告洗成不可采。

思维导图

先问：这份材料是不是“为了和解”才产生的？
NO
不是为和解而生 → FRE 408 不挡
再问
它是不是别的规则还会挡住？
本题 对方当事人自己的报告 → 非传闻 / 可采 → 可用于证明隐瞒
YES
若真是和解陈述，才会被 408 重点拦住
但本题事实 报告在施工期间已存在 → 后来只是拿去谈判 → 不能反向封口

考点陷阱

你可能会想：它是在 settlement negotiations 里拿出来的，所以整份报告都不能用。

但考试真正问的是：这份报告是不是本来就为了和解才生成的；如果不是，FRE 408 不会替它“补一层保护”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 report was created during construction，说明它不是为和解而生；FRE 408 不拦，且它还是对方当事人自己的报告，故可采。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则绝对化

✕ A: 把 all statements 绝对化了，误以为一沾谈判就全封。

❌ 法律适用 | 传闻规则误套

✕ B: 只盯 hearsay，忘了对方当事人陈述本来就可能不是传闻。

❌ 事实误判 | 生成目的偷换

✕ C: 把“在谈判中被拿出”偷换成“为和解而写”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看证据最初的生成目的，再查 FRE 408，最后补看传闻与对方当事人陈述。

考场速记

记住一句：408 挡的是“为和解而说、为和解而写”，不是“后来在和解里被拿出来的原始材料”。

下次先问一句：这份东西是“谈判产物”，还是“原本就存在的证据”。

reason.en: Triggers FRE 408 but only for settlement-related evidence and prohibited uses.
reason.zh: 触发联邦证据规则408，但仅限制与和解相关证据的特定使用目的。

reason.en: Its admissibility turns on when and why it was created, not merely when it was disclosed.
reason.zh: 可否采纳取决于制作时间与目的，而非仅取决于披露时点。

reason.en: Shows the report predates compromise negotiations and was not made for settlement.
reason.zh: 表明报告早于和解谈判，并非为和解而制作。

reason.en: Defines the substantive issue the plaintiff seeks to prove with the report.
reason.zh: 界定原告拟用该报告证明的实体争议点。

keywords.text: establish the issue of willful concealment

reason.en: This purpose implicates FRE 408's bar on proving validity of a disputed claim.
reason.zh: 该使用目的涉及408规则对证明争议请求可否成立的限制。

reason.en: Confirms negotiations occurred but does not itself immunize otherwise admissible evidence.
reason.zh: 确认存在谈判，但本身并不使原本可采纳的证据当然排除。

A.text: all statements made during settlement negotiations

reason.en: FRE 408 is limited and does not bar all settlement-related evidence.
reason.zh: 408规则有范围限制，并非和解谈判中的一切陈述都不可采纳。

reason.en: Assumes settlement context alone makes the report inadmissible.
reason.zh: 误以为只要出现在和解情境中就当然不可采纳。

reason.en: Distracts from FRE 408 by mischaracterizing a party-opponent statement as hearsay.
reason.zh: 用传闻规则干扰判断，误将对方当事人陈述当作传闻。

reason.en: Ignores that party-opponent statements offered against the party are nonhearsay.
reason.zh: 忽略向对方当事人提出的对方当事人陈述不属于传闻。

C.text: admissible when offered to prove the validity of a claim

reason.en: FRE 408 generally bars using settlement statements to prove claim validity.
reason.zh: 408规则通常禁止用和解谈判陈述证明请求可否成立。

D.text: created for purposes other than settlement negotiations

reason.en: States the limiting principle that keeps preexisting evidence outside FRE 408.
reason.zh: 点明既有证据因非为和解而制作而不受408排除。

reason.en: Requires checking other rules such as hearsay after 408 is inapplicable.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
Police received a tip from an informant that a man that lived on his street might be dealing drugs out of his home. An investigation was initiated in response to the informant's tip. During the investigation, an undercover officer purchased cocaine from the man at his home on multiple occasions. Police ultimately obtained a valid warrant to search the man's home and, while executing the warrant, found a large quantity of cocaine. The man was subsequently charged with knowingly possessing cocaine with the intent to distribute.
Prior to trial, the man requested disclosure of the identity of the informant and the contents of the informant's statement to police. The prosecutor refused to disclose the informant's identity and the substance of the informant's statement to police, claiming that both are privileged.
How should the court rule on the prosecutor's privilege claims?

choices.A: Both the identity of the informant and the contents of the informant's statement to police are privileged.
choices.B: Only the contents of the informant's statement to police are privileged.
choices.C: Only the identity of the informant is privileged.
choices.D: Neither the identity of the informant nor the contents of the informant's statement to police are privileged.

questions.explanation:
Government-informant privilege
DEPARTMENT
OF
JUSTICE
Informant's identity = protected from disclosure
Confidential informant
Contents of communications = not protected from disclosure
Statement by Confidential informant
Name of Informant:
Statement by Informant: I believe that drugs are being sold out of the home located in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The home is owned by [the defendant], who is a known drug dealer.

The government-informant privilege protects the government from being compelled to disclose the identity of informants. However, the privilege does not apply when:

  • the informant's identity is already known to the defendant, or
  • the defendant shows that the informant's identity is material to the establishment of a defense or otherwise necessary and essential to a fair determination of the case.

Here, the informant merely provided a tip that the defendant might be dealing drugs from his home. Police conducted an independent investigation that included undercover drug buys and a search warrant, and the informant was not involved in those events. The informant's identity is therefore not material to any defense the defendant might raise, so the government may withhold it (Choices B & D).

In addition, the privilege does not protect the contents of an informant's statement when disclosure of the contents would not reveal the informant's identity. Here, the substance of the informant's tip does not reveal who the informant is, so the government must disclose the contents (Choice A).

📌 Educational Objective

The government may withhold an informant's identity but must generally disclose the content of the informant's communications when disclosure of the content would not reveal the informant's identity.

📚 References
  • Roviaro v. United States, 353 U.S. 53, 61–62 (1957) (identity of informant must be disclosed when the informant's testimony is relevant and helpful to defense).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：政府线人特权（government-informant privilege）里，身份（identity）通常能保密，但沟通内容（contents of communication）若不会暴露身份，一般要披露。

三秒认题路径：

线人身份 → 能否保密 → 内容是否暴露身份 → 分开判断 → 选 C

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则就够了

政府线人特权（government-informant privilege）保护政府不被强迫披露线人的身份（identity），考场意思：线人是谁，默认可以藏起来。

但这不是把所有东西都盖住；如果只是披露陈述内容（contents），而且不会反推出线人是谁，内容通常不受特权保护，考场意思：话可以说，名字未必说。

这里线人只是报了一个“可能在卖毒品”的线索，后面真正查到毒品的是卧底买毒和搜查令，不是线人本人，所以身份不因本题事实而必须公开。

核心判例： Roviaro v. United States — 线人身份若对辩护有实质帮助才可能必须披露；本题达不到这个门槛。

思维导图

先问：政府想保的是哪一层？
第1层：线人身份（identity）？
通常可保密：默认不披露
第2层：线人陈述内容（contents）？
若内容不会暴露身份，内容不受特权挡住
本题卡点：线人只给线索，卧底买毒和搜查令是独立证据
所以：身份可藏，内容要交
结论：只保护身份，不保护本题这段可单独披露的内容
答案：C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是“informant”，那他说过的话和他的名字都应该一起保密。

但考试真正问的是：身份和内容要分开看，内容只要不会把人反推出去，就不一定受保护。

司法考试看的是「名字会不会被迫暴露」，而不是「这段话听起来是不是敏感」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干显示线人只提供了一个毒品线索，真正证据来自卧底买毒和搜查令，所以身份可保密、内容可披露。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把identity和内容一锅端，特权没这么宽。

❌ 法律适用 | 内容保密误判

✕ B: 只护内容不护身份，正好把规则说反了。

❌ 事实误判 | 线索来源偷换

✕ D: 看到独立调查就以为全不保密，漏了线人身份这一层。

这题建议用什么方法？

先拆成“身份”和“内容”两层，再看内容会不会反向暴露身份。

考场速记

记住一句：线人身份默认护，陈述内容看会不会暴露身份；能单独说出来的内容，通常不靠特权拦住。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A defendant is on trial for tax evasion. The prosecutor, seeking to establish the defendant's income by showing his expenditures, has asked the defendant's attorney to produce records showing only how much the defendant had paid his attorney in fees.
Should the demand for the attorney's fee records be upheld?

choices.A: No, because the records are protected by the attorney work-product doctrine.
choices.B: No, because the records are protected by the attorney-client privilege.
choices.C: Yes, because it calls for relevant information not within the attorney-client privilege.
choices.D: Yes, because the attorney-client privilege cannot be invoked to conceal evidence of a crime.

questions.explanation:
Attorney-client privileged communications (FRE 502)
Privileged Any communication between attorney & client:
  • made to obtain or provide legal assistance for client and
  • intended to be & kept confidential
Not privileged
  • Purely factual information
  • Client's identity (generally)
  • Existence of attorney-client relationship
  • Client's legal fees & other incidentals
  • Attorney's fee records
  • Business advice or opinions

FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence.

Attorney-client communications are privileged if they are (1) made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice and/or representation and (2) intended to be and kept confidential. As a result, communications that are merely incidental to providing legal advice or representation (eg, attorney's fee records) are not privileged (Choice B). These nonprivileged communications are therefore subject to disclosure, discovery, and admission in a legal proceeding so long as they are relevant to the case.

Here, the attorney's fee records are not privileged because they are merely incidental to the attorney's representation. And since they are relevant to the defendant's personal income and expenditures in this tax-evasion case, the demand for the attorney's fee records should be upheld.

(Choice A) The attorney work-product doctrine律师工作成果原则
保护律师或当事人为预期诉讼而准备的材料；不涵盖客户支付律师费用的金额。 protects materials prepared by an attorney or client in anticipation of litigation — eg, attorney's impressions, opinions, or research. But the amount a client paid his attorney for legal representation is outside the protection of this doctrine.

(Choice D) The attorney-client privilege can be invoked to conceal confidential communications regarding a past (not ongoing or planned) crime or fraud. But this privilege does not apply to records regarding attorney fees.

📌 Educational Objective

Attorney-client communications are privileged if (1) made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice/representation and (2) intended to be and kept confidential. Communications that are merely incidental to the client's legal representation do not fall within this privilege.

zh-choices.A: 不应支持，因为这些记录受到律师工作成果原则的保护。
zh-choices.B: 不应支持，因为这些记录受到律师-当事人特权的保护。
zh-choices.C: 应支持，因为它要求提供不属于律师-当事人特权范围内的相关信息。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师费记录一般不受律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护，因为它只是附带的事实信息，不是为了保密获取法律意见的沟通内容。

三秒认题路径：

律师费记录 → 只记金额 → 不是保密沟通 → 不属特权 → 可强制披露

核心法律规则

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）只保护：为获取或提供法律帮助而作出的沟通，而且当事人打算并确实保持保密。律师费记录（attorney fee records）通常只是代表关系中的附带事实，考场意思：它告诉你“付了多少钱”，不是“法律意见说了什么”。

所以，单纯的费用记录一般不在特权内，若又和案件中的收入、支出有关，通常就可以被要求披露。工作成果原则（work-product doctrine）保护的是为预期诉讼准备的材料，考场意思：它不是拿来挡住“客户付了律师多少钱”这种账目事实的。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题核心结论；本题直接用的是“律师费记录通常不受特权保护”的基础规则。

思维导图

这类信息是不是律师-当事人特权保护的沟通？
先看：是否为了获取/提供法律帮助，且本来要保密？
本题事实：只要律师费金额，它是附带账目信息，不是法律意见交流。
结论：不是特权沟通，直接死在“保密法律交流”这一关
结果：只要和案件相关，就能要求交出，答案选 Yes。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：律师费是跟律师关系有关的东西，所以应该都能用 attorney-client privilege 挡住。

但考试真正问的是：这份材料是不是“保密法律沟通”，不是它和律师有没有关系。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干只要的是律师已收取的费用记录，它只是附带事实，不是保密法律沟通，所以不在特权内，且和纳税人收入支出有关时可要求提交。

❌ 概念混淆 | 工作成果误判

✕ A: 把work-product doctrine套到账目信息上了。

❌ 事实误判 | 保密沟通偷换

✕ B: 把“和律师有关”偷换成“保密法律沟通”。

❌ 法律适用 | 犯罪例外乱套

✕ D: 这不是在问crime or fraud例外。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看材料是不是“保密法律沟通”，再看它只是账目事实还是特权内容。

考场速记

记住一句：律师费记录（attorney fee records）一般不是特权沟通，通常可披露；看到“只是付了多少钱”，先别把 attorney-client privilege 想得太大。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A plaintiff, the owner of a hardware store, sued her attorney for malpractice after losing a lawsuit involving a defective product that was sold by the hardware store. The plaintiff claims that the attorney negligently handled the defense because he lacked sufficient expertise. At trial, the plaintiff, seeking to establish the attorney's negligence, produced a letter written by the attorney to the plaintiff summarizing a commonly used litigation strategy that the attorney failed to use at trial. In response, the attorney plans to testify to communications that the attorney made in meetings with the plaintiff regarding an alternative defense strategy, which they agreed to pursue. The plaintiff objects to the attorney's testimony, invoking the attorney-client privilege.
Should the court uphold the client's privilege claim?

choices.A: No, because the attorney's professional relationship with the plaintiff has ended.
choices.B: No, because the statement is not protected by the attorney-client privilege.
choices.C: Yes, because only the client, as the holder of the privilege, can waive it.
choices.D: Yes, because the communications were made for the purpose of obtaining legal assistance and intended to be kept confidential.

questions.explanation:
Common exceptions to attorney-client privilege
Exception Use of attorney-client communication Disclosure compelled by
Crime-fraud Made to further ongoing or future crime/fraud Party seeking to discover information about crime/fraud
Deceased client Resolves dispute over deceased client's testamentary intent Attorney
Self-defense Used to defend against client's malpractice or ethical claim against attorney Attorney
Fiduciary Constitutes legal advice between corporate fiduciaries & corporation's attorney Stockholders
Joint representation Made during attorney's prior representation of joint clients Any joint client in subsequent litigation between joint clients

The attorney-client privilege protects confidential communications between an attorney and a client that were made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice or representation. However, one exception to this privilege applies to communications that are relevant to an ongoing dispute between the attorney and the client (eg, malpractice action). In such cases, the attorney may disclose any confidential communications that are relevant to the attorney's defense on the disputed issue without the client's consent.

Here, the attorney plans to testify about confidential communications that he made during meetings with the plaintiff (client) regarding an alternative defense strategy (legal advice). But since these communications are relevant to establishing the attorney's defense in this ongoing malpractice dispute, the attorney-client privilege does not apply (Choice D). Therefore, the court should deny the client's privilege claim.

(Choice A) The privilege remains in effect even after the attorney-client relationship has ended (as seen here) or the client dies. Therefore, this would not be a basis for denying the plaintiff's privilege claim.

(Choice C) The attorney-client privilege can be waived放弃（特免权） by the client directly or by an attorney or other agent acting with the client's authority. But here, the client's waiver is unnecessary since the attorney-client privilege does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Attorney-client communications are not privileged if they are relevant to an ongoing dispute between the attorney and the client. Therefore, the attorney may disclose these communications without the client's consent.
questions.zh-question:
一名原告，同时也是一家五金店的店主，在输掉了一场涉及其五金店售出的缺陷产品的诉讼后，以执业不当为由起诉了她的律师。原告声称，该律师因缺乏足够的专业知识而疏忽地处理了辩护。在审理中，原告为证明律师的过失，出示了一封由律师写给原告的信函，信中概述了一个律师未在庭审中使用的常用诉讼策略。作为回应，律师计划就其与原告在会面中商讨的、双方同意采用的替代辩护策略进行作证。原告援引律师-当事人特免权，反对律师的证词。

法院是否应支持当事人的特免权主张？

zh-choices.A: 不应支持，因为律师与原告的职业关系已经终止。
zh-choices.B: 不应支持，因为该陈述不受律师-当事人特免权的保护。
zh-choices.C: 应支持，因为只有作为特免权持有人的当事人才能放弃该权利。
zh-choices.D: 应支持，因为该沟通是为了获取法律建议而进行的，并且意图保密。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）在律师因其被告的恶意诉讼而为自己辩护时，能不能挡住相关沟通被披露。

三秒认题路径：

律师自保 → 旧沟通要说 → 涉及同案争议 → 例外启动 → 特权挡不住

核心法律规则

先记住规则，再套本题

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的是为了寻求法律建议而作出的、保密的律师与当事人沟通。可是一旦沟通与律师和当事人之间的现有争议有关，尤其是当事人起诉律师的恶意代理（malpractice），律师就可以为自己的抗辩披露那些相关沟通。

所以这题的关键不是“这段话原本是不是法律咨询”，而是“它现在是不是律师拿来防御这场恶意诉讼的内容”。只要答案是前者相关、后者需要，特权就会被这个例外挤掉，考试上不能再拿它当遮羞布。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题的实体结论；本题真正锁定的是“律师为回应与当事人的现有争议，可以披露相关沟通”的特权例外。

思维导图

先问：这段沟通本来受 律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege） 保护吗？
YES：原本是保密法律建议。
再问：现在是不是律师在应对当事人的 malpractice 诉讼？
YES：相关沟通可为自我辩护而披露。
卡死点：不是“能不能保密”，而是“能不能拿来替律师自己辩护”。
结果：特权不挡这份 testimony。
终点：选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这明明是律师和客户之间的保密谈话，而且律师关系已经结束了，应该还能继续挡住披露。

但考试真正问的是：这份沟通是不是被用来处理律师和客户之间的现有恶意诉讼；如果是，特权例外就会打开。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 律师要用这段沟通为自己抗辩，正落在恶意代理争议的例外里，所以它不受特权保护。

❌ 事实误判 | 结束关系误读

✕ A: 把 relationship has ended 当关键点了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 放弃规则误套

✕ C: 盯着 waive 不放，但这里根本不是在问谁放弃了特权。

❌ 法律适用 | 原始保密误判

✕ D: 只看到 confidential 和法律建议，却漏了“律师自保例外”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找是不是“律师对客户的现有争议”，再判断特权例外是否直接放行披露。

考场速记

记住一句：律师为自己辩护时，相关保密沟通可能可讲。遇到特权题，先问“原本是否保密”，再问“现在是不是落进例外”。

这题的速记就是：malpractice 一出现，先想“自保例外”；别被“原本是 legal advice”带跑。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A plaintiff brought a diversity action in State A federal court against a defendant, a spinal surgeon, alleging medical malpractice. The plaintiff claims that the defendant ignored established medical guidelines while performing a procedure on the plaintiff, causing her ongoing and debilitating back pain. The defendant contends that the plaintiff's back pain is attributable to her failure to follow recovery instructions. The defendant has filed a motion to compel production of medical records from the plaintiff's family physician that contain a statement by the plaintiff that her back pain began after she picked up her child against the defendant's recovery instructions. The plaintiff has objected, citing the physician-patient privilege recognized under State A law.
Should the court uphold the plaintiff's privilege claim?

choices.A: No, because the physician-patient privilege is not applicable in federal proceedings.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiff's physical condition is at issue.
choices.C: Yes, because State A recognizes the physician-patient privilege.
choices.D: Yes, provided the statement was made for the purpose of obtaining medical treatment.

questions.explanation:
Physician-patient privilege
Applicability Not recognized by federal common law, which applies in federal-question suits. Typically recognized by state law, which applies in federal diversity suits.
Scope Protects confidential communications between patient & physician made for purpose of obtaining medical treatment unless:
  • patient's physical condition is at issue
  • communication was part of crime or tort
  • dispute between physician & patient
  • patient contractually waived privilege
Privilege holder Patient holds privilege until his/her death, then privilege terminates.

The physician-patient privilege protects confidential communications between a patient and a physician made for the purpose of obtaining medical treatment. Federal common law, which generally governs privilege claims in federal court, does not recognize this privilege. But state rules on privilege must be applied when a federal suit is based on diversity jurisdiction (as seen here). Since State A recognizes the physician-patient privilege, it could apply in this federal diversity action (Choice A).

However, even when recognized by state law, the physician-patient privilege is inapplicable in the following circumstances:

  • the patient's physical condition is at issue
  • the communication was part of the commission of a crime or tort
  • a dispute exists between the physician and patient or
  • the patient contractually waived the privilege.

Here, the plaintiff's physical condition is at issue because she alleges that her back pain was caused by the defendant's failure to follow established medical guidelines. The statements in the family physician's medical records are relevant to this issue because they suggest that the pain instead resulted from the plaintiff's failure to follow recovery instructions. Therefore, the plaintiff's privilege claim should not be upheld (Choices C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

The physician-patient privilege, if recognized by state law, applies in federal diversity suits unless:

  • (1) the patient's physical condition is at issue,
  • (2) the patient-physician communication was part of a crime or tort,
  • (3) there is a dispute between the patient and physician, or
  • (4) the patient contractually waived the privilege.
📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (privileges).

一名原告在A州联邦法院对一名被告（脊柱外科医生）提起了多样性管辖诉讼，指控其医疗事故。原告声称，被告在为原告实施手术时，无视既定的医疗准则，导致其持续性且使人衰弱的背部疼痛。被告辩称，原告的背部疼痛是由于其未能遵守康复指示所致。被告已提交一份强制动议，要求原告的家庭医生出示其医疗记录，该记录中包含原告的一项陈述，即她的背部疼痛是在违反被告的康复指示抱起孩子后开始的。原告以A州法律承认的医患特免权为由提出反对。

法院是否应支持原告的特免权主张？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为医患特免权不适用于联邦诉讼程序。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为原告的身体状况已成为争议点。
zh-choices.C: 应该，因为A州承认医患特免权。
zh-choices.D: 应该，前提是该陈述是为了获得医疗为目的而作出的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州法承认的医患特权（physician-patient privilege），在联邦多元管辖案件里，遇到“病人身体状况本身就是争点”时，能不能挡住强制披露令。

三秒认题路径：

多元诉讼 → 州特权规则 → 身体状况争点 → 例外命中 → 不能挡披露

核心法律规则

医患特权（physician-patient privilege）保护的是为了接受治疗而向医生做出的保密沟通，所以它不是“所有病历都绝对保密”。联邦普通法（federal common law）一般不认这个特权，但在多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction）里要用州法；所以这里州A认这个特权，原则上可以适用。

但这题一碰到例外就直接倒下：只要患者的身体状况（physical condition）本身就是争点，这个特权通常就不能用来挡住相关医疗记录。考试上你要盯的是“这份记录是不是在帮法官判断背痛到底从哪来”，不是盯着“州法有没有这个特权”本身。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题；本题锁定的是州法医患特权的例外规则：身体状况一旦成为争点，特权就让位。

思维导图

先问：这是联邦法院里的特权争议吗？
YES多元管辖 → 用州特权法
再问：州法医患特权能不能罩住这份病历？
默认：为了治疗的保密沟通，通常可挡披露
关键门槛：身体状况（physical condition）是不是争点？
卡死点：是。背痛原因正是诉讼焦点，记录正拿来证明或反驳病因。
结论：特权例外命中 → 不能用特权拒绝动议。
NO若不是州法特权问题，就换别的证据规则分析。
答案落点：B，因为这不是“有没有特权”，而是“特权被例外打穿了”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州A既然承认医患特权（physician-patient privilege），那病历就该自动保密。

但考试真正问的是：这个特权有没有被“身体状况争点”这个例外打掉。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以这里不是在比“谁更隐私”，而是在看这份记录是不是正好用来判断背痛成因；一旦是，特权就不保了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 back pain is at issue，病历内容正用来判断背痛成因，所以州法特权被例外打穿，不能挡这份披露。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把联邦普通法和多元案件混成一团了。

❌ 法律适用 | 州法万能误判

✕ C: 只看到州A承认特权，漏掉了身体状况例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 治疗目的偷换

✕ D: 把 purpose of obtaining medical treatment 当成决定性条件了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看联邦还是州法，再立刻查特权例外，别被“州里承认”四个字带偏。

考场速记

记住这句：州法特权在多元诉讼里可能进来，但一旦病人身体状况就是争点，特权常常立刻失效。

考场口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 不是本题重点；本题真正要背的是“身体状况争点 → 医患特权例外”。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A defendant is charged with conspiracy to sell and distribute cocaine. The defendant's attorney contacted the prosecutor to enter plea negotiations. The prosecutor stated that the defendant would first have to agree that any statements made by the defendant during negotiations could be used to impeach him at trial in the event that a plea bargain could not be reached. After deliberating with his attorney, the defendant agreed to proceed under those terms, but the negotiations were fruitless.
At trial, the defendant testified as to his lack of involvement in the alleged conspiracy. The prosecutor now seeks to cross-examine the defendant about a contrary statement that he made during plea discussions.
Is the proposed cross-examination proper?

choices.A: No, because statements made during plea negotiations cannot be used to impeach a defendant.
choices.B: No, because the protections for statements made during plea negotiations are not subject to waiver.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant and the prosecutor did not reach a plea bargain.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant knowingly and voluntarily agreed to waive any protections.

questions.explanation:
Pleas, plea discussions & related statements (FRE 410)

NOT admissible against defendant:
  • Withdrawn guilty plea
  • Nolo contendere (ie, no contest) plea
  • Statements made during proceeding on above pleas
  • Statements made during plea discussions with prosecuting attorney
Knowingly & voluntarily waives protection
Exceptions:
  • Another statement during same plea/discussion is introduced & statements should be considered together
  • Criminal proceeding for perjury or false statement if statement made under oath, on record & with counsel present
Admissible
FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence.

The law encourages settlement of disputes and plea-bargaining, so statements made during settlement or plea negotiations are generally not admissible against a defendant who participated in the negotiations or made the plea. However, a defendant may waive this protection - just like any other privilege - if the waiver is made knowingly and voluntarily (Choice B).

Here, the statements that the defendant made during plea negotiations would typically be inadmissible at trial. However, the defendant knowingly and voluntarily waived this protection after deliberating with his attorney. And since the defendant's waiver allows the prosecutor to use any statements made during plea negotiations to impeach the defendant's trial testimony, the prosecutor's proposed cross-examination is proper.

(Choice A) Statements made during plea negotiations generally cannot be used against the defendant for any purpose - including impeachment. However, this protection is lost once it has been waived (as seen here).

(Choice C) The rule excluding statements made during plea negotiations applies even when a plea bargain was not reached. Otherwise, the negotiating parties would be penalized if no agreement was reached, which would discourage the settlement of disputes.

📌 Educational Objective

Statements made during settlement or plea negotiations are generally inadmissible against a defendant who participated in the negotiations or made the plea. However, a defendant may waive this protection if the waiver is made knowingly and voluntarily.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 410 (prohibited use of pleas, plea discussions, and related statements).
  • United States v. Mezzanatto, 513 U.S. 196, 210 (1995) (upholding a criminal defendant's agreement to waive the protections afforded under the plea-statement rules if the agreement was made knowingly and voluntarily).

一名被告被指控共谋销售和分销可卡因。被告的律师联系了检察官进行认罪协商。检察官表示，被告必须首先同意，如果无法达成认罪协议，其在协商期间所作的任何陈述都可以在庭审中用以弹劾他。在与律师商议后，被告同意在这些条款下进行协商，但协商无果而终。

在庭审中，被告作证称其未参与所指控的共谋。检察官现在试图就其在认罪协商期间所作的相反陈述对被告进行交叉询问。

该提议的交叉询问是否适当？

zh-choices.A: 不适当，因为在认罪协商期间所作的陈述不能用以弹劾被告。
zh-choices.B: 不适当，因为对认罪协商期间所作陈述的保护不得被放弃。
zh-choices.C: 适当，因为被告和检察官未达成认罪协议。
zh-choices.D: 适当，因为被告明知且自愿地同意放弃任何保护。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Public policy exclusions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：认罪协商（plea discussions）中的陈述本来受 FRE 410 保护，但被告若已知情且自愿（knowingly and voluntarily）放弃，该保护就能被用来弹劾。

三秒认题路径：

认罪协商 → 默认排除 → 看放弃 → 知情自愿 → 可交叉询问

核心法律规则

认罪协商陈述（statements made during plea discussions）一般不能对被告使用，考场意思：你不能因为谈判失败就把他说过的话直接拿来打他。

但被告可以像放弃别的证据保护一样，知情且自愿（knowingly and voluntarily）地放弃这层保护；一旦放弃，检方就能把这些话拿来弹劾。这里的关键不是有没有谈成，而是有没有有效放弃。

核心判例： United States v. Mezzanatto — 认罪协商保护可以被被告知情且自愿地放弃，因此谈判中的陈述可按约定用于弹劾。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 FRE 410 保护的谈判陈述？
是默认不能拿来对被告使用，也不能因为plea bargain 没谈成就自动失效。
再看被告有没有知情且自愿（knowingly and voluntarily）放弃保护？
有放弃 → 保护失效 → 这些话可用于弹劾 → 选 D
别被骗“没达成协议”不是突破口；真正卡死点是“有没有有效 waiver”。
一句话收尾：先找 FRE 410，再找 waiver，最后看能不能用来 impeach。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然双方最后没谈成，检方当然不能用这些话。

但考试真正问的是：被告有没有已经把这层保护知情且自愿地让出去。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「谈判内容有没有让他吃亏」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干最关键的事实是被告在律师商量后知情且自愿同意，所以 FRE 410 的保护已经被放弃，检方可用该陈述弹劾他。

❌ 概念混淆 | 绝对排除误判

✕ A: 把 cannot be used 误当成绝对禁令，漏看了可放弃这一步。

❌ 法律适用 | 放弃效力误判

✕ B: 误以为这类保护天生不能放弃，not subject to waiver 这句会把你带偏。

❌ 事实误判 | 未成交偷换

✕ C: 把“没谈成”偷换成“可使用”，其实谈判失败不等于失去排除保护。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 FRE 410 的默认排除，再只问一个问题：有没有有效 waiver。

考场速记

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A defendant has pleaded not guilty to a federal bank robbery charge.
The principal issue at trial is the identity of the robber. The prosecutor has called the defendant's wife to testify to the clothing that the defendant wore as he left their house on the day the bank was robbed, expecting her description to match that of eyewitnesses to the robbery. Both the defendant and his wife have objected to her testifying against the defendant.
Should the wife be required to testify?

choices.A: No, because the defendant has a privilege to prevent his wife from testifying against him in a criminal case.
choices.B: No, because the wife has a privilege not to testify against her husband in a criminal case.
choices.C: Yes, because the spousal testimonial privilege does not apply in criminal cases.
choices.D: Yes, because the wife's viewing of the defendant's clothing was not a confidential communication.

questions.explanation:
Spousal communications v. Spousal immunity
Before marriage During marriage After marriage
Spousal communications (both spouses)
Spousal immunity (witness-spouses)
Protected communications
Duration of privilege

Two common law privileges apply to spousal testimony when in federal court:

  • Spousal-communications privilege – protects confidential communications between spouses during the marriage from disclosure in a civil or criminal case, even after the marriage has ended
  • Spousal-immunity (ie, spousal-testimonial) privilege – protects persons in an active marriage from testifying against their spouse in a criminal case about any matters that occurred before or during the marriage (Choice C)

The witness-spouse holds the spousal-immunity privilege and therefore has the unilateral right to either (1) refuse to testify against the other spouse or (2) waive the privilege and testify.

Here, the wife holds the spousal-immunity privilege because she is the testifying spouse. Therefore, the defendant cannot prevent her from testifying against him in his criminal prosecution for bank robbery (Choice A). Nor can the prosecution require her to do so.

(Choice D) The spousal-communications privilege allows either spouse to refuse to disclose or prevent the other from disclosing confidential communications—not mere observations (eg, noticing a spouse's clothing). But the wife need not testify if she asserts the spousal-immunity privilege.

📌 Educational Objective

The spousal-communications privilege protects confidential communications during the marriage from disclosure in a civil or criminal case. In contrast, the spousal-immunity privilege protects persons from being required to testify against their spouse in a criminal case about events that occurred before or during the marriage.

📚 References
  • Trammel v. United States, 445 U.S. 40, 53 (1980) (vesting spousal-immunity privilege in the witness-spouse).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (privileges).

是否应要求该妻子作证？

zh-choices.A: 不应要求，因为在刑事案件中，被告享有阻止其妻子作出对他不利证言的特权。
zh-choices.B: 不应要求，因为在刑事案件中，妻子享有不作出对其丈夫不利证言的特权。
zh-choices.C: 应要求，因为配偶证言特权不适用于刑事案件。
zh-choices.D: 应要求，因为妻子看到被告的衣物并非一项保密通信。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：配偶免证特权（spousal-immunity privilege）由谁持有，能不能让正在作证的妻子在联邦刑事案里拒绝作证。

三秒认题路径：

已婚夫妻 → 刑事案 → 妻子作证 → 看免证特权 → 只能她自己决定

核心法律规则

这一题只看两种特权

配偶通信特权（spousal-communications privilege）保护婚姻存续期间的保密交流，考场意思：别人不能逼你们把“说过的话”交出来。

配偶免证特权（spousal-immunity privilege）保护仍在婚姻中的证人配偶（witness-spouse）拒绝在刑事案里作证，考场意思：她自己可以说“我不证”，但被告丈夫不能替她做决定。

本题里妻子只是看到丈夫穿什么衣服，不是保密交流；但她作为证人配偶，仍可直接拒绝替丈夫作证，所以答案走“不能强迫她上庭”这条线。

核心判例： Trammel v. United States —— 把配偶免证特权锁定在证人配偶手里，所以被告不能单方面阻止妻子作证。

思维导图

先问：这是要不要立刻作证的问题吗？
NO 继续看：妻子是不是证人配偶（witness-spouse）？
YES 她在有效婚姻中作证，免证特权在她手里，不在丈夫手里。
再分 讨论的是“衣服长什么样”→ 这不是保密交流（confidential communication），所以配偶通信特权（spousal-communications privilege）也帮不上忙。
结论 妻子若选择不证，法庭不能逼她；丈夫也不能替她挡。
最后落点：选 B，因为“她有权不作证”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然丈夫不同意，法院就不能让妻子开口。

但考试真正问的是：谁持有这个特权，答案是证人配偶本人，不是被告配偶。

司法考试看的是「谁能在程序上决定要不要证」，而不是「丈夫愿不愿意她说」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键是妻子正在被要求在刑事案中作证，配偶免证特权（spousal-immunity privilege）在她手里，所以她可以拒绝。

❌ 概念混淆 | 夫妻权利错位

✕ A: 把特权当成丈夫的控制权了，prevent his wife 不是规则。

❌ 法律适用 | 免证规则反说

✕ C: 直接把配偶免证特权说没了，和题干的婚姻存续情形正相反。

❌ 事实误判 | 把观察当交流

✕ D: 只盯着confidential communication，忽略了本题先卡的是免证特权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“谁持有特权”，再分清“不能作证”和“不能泄密”这两条线。

考场速记

记住一句：spousal-immunity 看证人配偶自己愿不愿意上；spousal-communications 才看有没有保密交流。

这题的口诀就是：“能不能不证，看她自己；说过的话能不能藏，才看通信特权。”

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
In a suit against the defendant, the plaintiff sought to subpoena an audiotape on which the defendant had narrated his version of the dispute for his attorney. Counsel for the defendant moves to quash the subpoena on the ground of privilege.
In which of the following circumstances is the audiotape most likely to be subject to subpoena?

choices.A: The defendant has been deposed and there is good reason to believe that the audiotape may contain inconsistent statements.
choices.B: The defendant is deceased and thus unavailable to give testimony in person.
choices.C: The defendant played the audiotape for his father to get his reactions.
choices.D: The lawsuit involved alleged criminal behavior by the defendant.

questions.explanation:
Waiving attorney-client privilege

Waiver No waiver
  • voluntarily disclosing information to third party
  • voluntarily giving up privilege (eg, contractually)
  • failing to timely claim privilege (eg, after inadvertent disclosure)
  • failing to object to another's disclosure of confidential information
  • client's death
  • termination of attorney-client relationship

A subpoena传票：法院命令某人出庭作证或出示文件的司法文书。 can be quashed if it requests information protected from disclosure by a privilege特免权：允许拒绝披露某些保密信息的法律保护。. For example, the attorney-client privilege protects communications that are (1) made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice and/or representation and (2) intended to be and kept confidential. This privilege remains intact unless the client waives it — eg, by voluntarily disclosing the information to a third party.

Here, the defendant's audiotaped version of the dispute is privileged because he gave it to his attorney to obtain legal advice and presumably intended that it be kept confidential. But the defendant would waive this privilege if he voluntarily played the audiotape for his father, thereby disclosing its contents to a third party. And in such circumstances, the audiotape would likely be subject to subpoena.

(Choice A) Good reason to believe that an item might contain statements inconsistent with a witness's sworn testimony is not a basis to overcome a valid claim of privilege.

(Choice B) A defendant's availability has no impact on the ability to subpoena privileged information. Therefore, the defendant's audiotaped narration remains privileged even after his death.

(Choice D) Attorney-client communications made to further an ongoing or future crime are not privileged. But here, the lawsuit concerns a past dispute. So even if the lawsuit involved the defendant's alleged criminal behavior, his audiotaped narration of that dispute for his attorney is privileged.

📌 Educational Objective

The attorney-client privilege protects communications made to obtain legal advice and/or representation when they are intended to be and kept confidential. But a client can waive the privilege by voluntarily disclosing protected information to a third party.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (federal common law privileges).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）是否因向第三人主动展示而放弃，所以重点不是内容有没有不利，而是有没有 waiver（放弃特权）。

三秒认题路径：

律师咨询材料 → 默认保密 → 是否给第三人看 → 一旦外泄 → 特权失效

核心法律规则

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的是为了获取法律意见而与律师沟通、并且本来打算保密的内容。考场意思：只要客户把受保护内容主动给了第三人看，通常就等于自己把特权放弃了。

特权不会因为当事人后来死亡而自动消失；也不会因为对方觉得材料“可能有矛盾”就被突破。ongoing or future crime（正在进行或未来犯罪）才可能打掉特权，但本题是过去争议，不是那条例外。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter — 律师-当事人特权的披露命令通常不满足附带命令原则，等终局后仍可救济，所以一般不能立刻上诉。

思维导图

先看：这是不是“强制披露受特权材料”的命令？
是 进入附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）审查
三要件里，关键是“现在不立刻上诉，会不会以后根本救不回来”
本题卡点
有效复审（effectively reviewable）没过：终局后还能撤销、重审、排除错误披露材料
结论 不能立刻上诉，回到特权本身：若客户主动给第三人看，特权已放弃，材料可被传票取得
再问 这份材料原本是不是为法律意见而准备、并 intended to be confidential？
是 默认受保护
但如果 主动给父亲等第三人看
放弃（waiver）成立，特权被自己打掉
答案 选 C：主动向第三人披露后，传票更可能成立

考点陷阱

你可能会想：只要材料里可能有“前后不一致”，或者当事人已经死亡，法院就该放行让人拿到。

但考试真正问的是：有没有 waiver（放弃），不是对方有没有找到更想看的理由。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 主动给父亲看 这一事实就是向第三人披露，直接触发 waiver（放弃特权），所以这份录音最可能被传票调取。

❌ 事实误判 | 矛盾推断误判

✕ A: 盯着 inconsistent statements 也没用，特权不是靠“内容可疑”就能打穿。

❌ 概念混淆 | 死亡失权误判

✕ B: 把当事人去世当成特权自动消失，错；死亡本身不等于放弃。

❌ 法律适用 | 犯罪例外误判

✕ D: 看到 criminal behavior 就套犯罪例外，但本题是过去争议的咨询材料，不是促成犯罪。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否保密沟通”，再查“是否主动给第三人看”，最后才看别的干扰事实。

考场速记

记住一句：律师-当事人特权先看“为法律意见而保密”，再看有没有自己把内容给第三人看；一旦外泄，通常就是 waiver（放弃）。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A corporation's in-house legal department initiated an internal investigation after being informed of potential misconduct involving payments made to government officials. As part of the investigation, an attorney from the legal department interviewed every member of the corporation's accounting department responsible for making such payments. The attorney took detailed notes of the accountants' statements and her corresponding mental impressions. Upon completing the internal investigation, the corporation's legal department informed the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) of the payments. The IRS then opened an investigation into the legality of such payments and now seeks the production of the interview notes. The corporation's legal counsel has objected on the ground of privilege.
Which portion of the notes, if any, is likely privileged?

choices.A: All of the notes are privileged.
choices.B: Only the portion concerning the accountants' statements is privileged.
choices.C: Only the portion containing the attorney's mental impressions is privileged.
choices.D: None of the notes are privileged, provided that the IRS can show a substantial need for the notes and cannot otherwise obtain them without undue hardship.

questions.explanation:
Attorney-client privilege for corporate clients
Control-group test
(minority state view)		 Confidential communication* privileged if it:
  • was received from employee in position of control or who takes substantial part in decision-making
Federal standard
(& majority state view)		 Confidential communication* privileged if it:
  • was made by any employee for express purpose of securing legal advice for corporation and
  • related to employee's specific corporate duties
*A communication is confidential if it was intended to be & was kept confidential.

The attorney-client privilege protects confidential communications between an attorney and a client made for the purpose of seeking legal advice or representation. When an attorney represents a corporate client, some states limit this privilege to communications received from employees in a position of control or who take a substantial part in decision-making (ie, the "control group"). However, federal law extends this privilege to communications from non-control-group employees if the communication concerned matters within the employee's corporate duties and was made for the purpose of securing legal advice for the corporation.

Here, the attorney's notes include statements made by employees in the corporation's accounting department. Although these employees may not be part of the "control group," the statements concern payments made to government officials — a matter that likely is within the accountants' corporate duties. And since the accountants presumably knew that they were being interviewed so that the corporation could obtain legal advice about those payments, the communications contained in the notes are likely privileged (Choices C & D).

However, the attorney's mental impressions are not covered by the attorney-client privilege; they are protected by the attorney work-product privilege. Under this doctrine, ordinary work product (eg, witness statements) is discoverable if the requesting party shows a substantial need for the information and cannot otherwise obtain it without undue hardship. But opinion work product (eg, mental impressions) is discoverable only in rare instances. Therefore, the portion containing the attorney's mental impressions is likely privileged too (Choices B & D).

📌 Educational Objective

For corporate clients, federal law extends the attorney-client privilege to confidential communications from any employee that (1) concerned matters within the employee's corporate duties and (2) were made for the purpose of securing legal advice for the corporation.

📚 References
  • Upjohn Co. v. United States, 449 U.S. 383, 394 (1981) (extending attorney-client privilege to employee communications concerning matters within the employee's corporate duties made to obtain legal advice for the corporation).

这些笔记的哪一部分（若有）可能享有特免权？

zh-choices.A: 所有笔记都享有特免权。
zh-choices.B: 只有涉及会计师陈述的部分享有特免权。
zh-choices.C: 只有包含律师心理印象的部分享有特免权。
zh-choices.D: 所有笔记都不享有特免权，前提是 IRS 能够证明对这些笔记有重大需求，并且无法在不承受过度困难的情况下通过其他方式获取。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：公司内部调查中，员工访谈笔记里的律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）范围，是否连同律师的意见一起保护。

三秒认题路径：

公司调查 → 员工访谈 → 保密取法顾 → 先看特权 → 选 A

核心法律规则

这题只抓这一条

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的是为取得法律意见而作出的保密沟通，所以公司员工只要是在自己的具体岗位职责（corporate duties）范围内，且是为了帮公司拿到法律建议而接受访谈，内容通常都受保护。

对公司客户，联邦标准比少数州的control-group test更宽，不只保护“控制层”员工；像这里会计部门就政府付款接受调查，和律师说的话如果是保密的，就会落入特权。

但律师的mental impressions不是这道题要用的特权分析重点；题干问的是能否生产整份笔记，先看这些笔记是否本身属于保密法律沟通。

核心判例： Upjohn Co. v. United States —— 公司内部调查时，员工关于其岗位事务的保密访谈内容，也能进入律师-当事人特权保护范围。

思维导图

内部调查 公司发现可疑付款
→
律师访谈 问会计部门
→
保密沟通 为取得法律意见
→
联邦规则 不只看 control group
→
结果 整份笔记受保护
看见“员工访谈 + 为取法律意见 + 保密” → 直接想到 Upjohn
先排除：不是只问“谁是高层”。
卡死点：公司特权不只护管理层，员工关于岗位事务的保密沟通也能护。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：会计不是公司的“控制层”，所以他们说的话都不受特权保护。

但考试真正问的是：这些话是不是为了帮公司拿法律意见而作的保密沟通，不是员工职级高不高。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的会计部门访谈是为公司获取法律意见而做的保密沟通，按 Upjohn，整份笔记都可能落入特权。

❌ 概念混淆 | 控制层误判

✕ B: 把control group当成唯一标准，漏掉联邦规则更宽。

❌ 法律适用 | 工作成果错位

✕ C: 把mental impressions单独拎出来，忽略题目先问的是特权覆盖整份访谈笔记。

❌ 事实误判 | 硬套例外条件

✕ D: 先把substantial need搬进来，但这组笔记的核心不是普通工作成果那条路。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是公司内部保密访谈，再直接套 Upjohn，别被“是不是管理层”带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：公司访谈先想 Upjohn，看“岗位事务 + 取法律意见 + 保密”这三件事；不是控制层也可能受护。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A man was prosecuted in federal court for making threats against the President of the United States. The man was a voluntary patient in a private psychiatric hospital and told a nurse, shortly before the President came to town, that he planned to shoot the President. The nurse reported the threat to FBI agents. The man filed a motion to prevent the nurse from testifying.
Is the man's motion likely to be granted?

choices.A: No, because the man had not been committed involuntarily by court order.
choices.B: No, because the statement was not within any privilege.
choices.C: Yes, because the nurse violated a confidence in reporting the statement.
choices.D: Yes, because the statement was made in a medical setting.

questions.explanation:
Psychotherapist-patient privilege
Confidential communication between psychotherapist/social worker & patient protected if made during the course of diagnosis or treatment of mental/emotional condition unless:
  • patient's mental condition at issue
  • communication made during court-ordered mental exam or
  • communication introduced at involuntary-commitment proceeding
Patient holds privilege & psychotherapist must assert in patient's absence

A privilege protects confidential communications from disclosure, discovery, or admission in a legal proceeding. Under Federal Rule of Evidence 501, claims of privilege are generally governed by the common law.* For instance, the common law psychotherapist-patient privilege protects confidential communications between a psychotherapist (ie, a psychologist or psychiatrist) or social worker and a patient made during the course of treatment or diagnosis.

Here, the psychotherapist-patient privilege is implicated because the man is a patient in a psychiatric hospital. But his statement — ie, the threat against the President — does not fall within that privilege because it was not made to a psychotherapist or social worker OR during treatment or diagnosis. Therefore, though the nurse may have violated a confidence in reporting the statement, the man's motion is unlikely to be granted (Choice C).

*Common law governs claims of privilege in federal court unless (1) the Constitution, a federal statute, or a rule provides otherwise or (2) the suit is based on diversity jurisdiction多元管辖权：当案件基于州籍多样性时，联邦法院须适用州法律（包括州的特免权规则）。 so state rules on privilege must be applied.

(Choice A) Involuntary commitment is not required to protect a confidential communication under the psychotherapist-patient privilege.

(Choice D) The statement was made in a medical setting. But this alone is not a basis to prevent the nurse from testifying about the man's threat against the President.

📌 Educational Objective

The psychotherapist-patient privilege applies to confidential communications (1) between a psychotherapist/social worker and a patient (2) made during the course of treatment or diagnosis.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (privilege in general).

一名男子因威胁美国总统而在联邦法院被起诉。该男子是一家私立精神病院的自愿入院患者，在总统来到该市前不久，他告诉一名护士，他计划枪杀总统。护士将此威胁报告给了联邦调查局（FBI）特工。该男子提出动议，要求禁止该护士作证。

该男子的动议是否可能被批准？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该男子并非由法院命令非自愿收治。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该陈述不在任何特免权的保护范围内。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为护士报告该陈述违反了保密义务。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该陈述是在医疗环境中作出的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：精神科特权（psychotherapist-patient privilege）只保护“治疗或诊断过程中的保密沟通”，不是“在医院里说过的话”都能封口。

三秒认题路径：

医院里说话 → 先看特权对象 → 再看治疗/诊断 → 不满足就外露 → 不能拦证言

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则就够了

联邦法院里，特权一般看普通法（common law），考场意思：先问这句话有没有被某种特权罩住。精神科特权（psychotherapist-patient privilege）只保护心理治疗师、精神科医生或社会工作者与患者之间、在治疗或诊断（treatment or diagnosis）过程中形成的保密沟通。

本题里，男人把威胁说给的是护士（nurse），不是特权覆盖的对象；而且这句话也不是在治疗或诊断沟通中形成，所以根本进不了这个特权门槛。involuntary commitment不是启动该特权的必要条件，医院环境本身也不等于特权。

核心判例： Jaffee v. Redmond 锁定精神科特权的范围：要看“谁在说、对谁说、在什么目的下说”，不是只看是不是医疗场景。

思维导图

先问：这句话是不是被特权保护？
NO 1：说话对象是 nurse，不是心理治疗师/精神科医生/社会工作者。
NO 2：内容是对总统的威胁，不是为了 treatment or diagnosis 的保密沟通。
卡死点：privilege 门槛没进，护士当然可以作证。
误区：别把“在精神病院说的”偷换成“自动保密”。
结论：不能阻止护士证言 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他在精神科医院里说的，又是病人身份，应该当然保密。

但考试真正问的是：这句话有没有落进精神科特权（psychotherapist-patient privilege）的保护范围，而不是它听起来像不像“医疗隐私”。

司法考试看的是「法律上有没有特权」，而不是「物理上是不是在医院里说的」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 对护士说的威胁 既不是特权对象，也不是治疗或诊断中的保密沟通，所以不受保护，不能拦住护士作证。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 involuntary 误当必要条件了。

❌ 法律适用 | 证人身份误判

✕ C: 只看“有保密感”，却忽略护士不是特权主体。

❌ 事实误判 | 医疗场景偷换

✕ D: 把 medical setting 当成自动特权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“说给谁听、为啥说”，再决定特权有没有门槛内命中。

考场速记

记住一句：精神科特权不是“医院里说话就保密”，而是“特定专业人士 + 治疗或诊断中的保密沟通”。

本题快速口令：who / why / when 三问过不去，就别幻想特权能挡证言。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A plaintiff, a national restaurant chain, brought a trademark infringement suit against the owner of a small eatery. The plaintiff claims that the owner willfully traded on the plaintiff's registered mark, causing customers to associate the eatery's inferior food with the plaintiff's restaurants.
The plaintiff has filed a motion to compel production of two sets of emails that were sent prior to the lawsuit. In the first set of emails, the owner notes the similarities between its logo and the plaintiff's and asks his attorney for an opinion on potential trademark infringement liability. The attorney never responded. In the second set of emails, both the owner and the attorney discuss the eatery's business potential, given its highly recognizable logo. The owner objects, citing the attorney-client privilege.
How should the court rule on the owner's privilege claim?

choices.A: Both sets of emails are privileged.
choices.B: Only the first set of emails is privileged, because the second set of emails does not provide legal advice.
choices.C: Only the second set of emails email is privileged, because the first set of emails does not include the attorney's response.
choices.D: Neither set of emails is privileged, because both tend to establish willful trading on the plaintiff's mark.

questions.explanation:
Attorney-client privileged communications (FRE 502)
Privileged Any communication between attorney & client:
  • made to obtain or provide legal assistance for client and
  • intended to be & kept confidential
Not privileged
  • Purely factual information
  • Client's identity (generally)
  • Existence of attorney-client relationship
  • Client's legal fees & other incidentals
  • Attorney's fee records
  • Business advice or opinions

FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence.

The attorney-client privilege protects confidential communications† that are made for the purpose of obtaining or providing legal assistance for the client. This allows the client to freely and frankly communicate with an attorney (and vice versa). As a result, the first set of emails in which the owner sought legal advice regarding the eatery's potential liability for trademark infringement is protected by this privilege (Choice C).

In contrast, attorney-client communications that are made for some other purpose are not protected by this privilege. This includes communications in which the client solicits, or the attorney offers, mere business advice or opinions. Therefore, the second set of emails about the eatery's business potential—which solicited business advice rather than legal advice—is not protected by this privilege (Choice A).

†Communications are confidential if they were intended to be and kept private.

(Choice D) The fact that both sets of emails tend to establish that the owner willfully traded on the plaintiff's mark has no bearing on the applicability of the attorney-client privilege. Instead, this privilege turns on whether the communication was made to obtain legal advice/representation.

📌 Educational Objective

The attorney-client privilege protects confidential communications that are made for the purpose of obtaining or providing legal assistance for the client. But communications made for other purposes—including rendering business advice or opinions—are not protected.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (federal common law privileges).
questions.zh-question:
原告是一家全国连锁餐厅，对一家小餐馆的业主提起了商标侵权诉讼。原告声称，该业主故意利用原告的注册商标，导致顾客将该餐馆品质较差的食物与原告的餐厅联系起来。

原告已提起一项动议，要求强制出示在诉讼前发送的两组电子邮件。在第一组电子邮件中，业主指出了其标志与原告标志的相似之处，并就潜在的商标侵权责任征求其律师的意见。律师从未回复。在第二组电子邮件中，业主和律师讨论了该餐馆凭借其高辨识度的标志所具有的商业潜力。业主以律师-当事人特免权为由提出异议。

法院应如何就业主的特免权主张作出裁定？

zh-choices.A: 两组电子邮件均享有特免权。
zh-choices.B: 只有第一组电子邮件享有特免权，因为第二组电子邮件未提供法律意见。
zh-choices.C: 只有第二组电子邮件享有特免权，因为第一组电子邮件不包含律师的回复。
zh-choices.D: 两组电子邮件均不享有特免权，因为它们都倾向于证实业主故意利用了原告的商标。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）只保护为获取或提供法律帮助而作的保密沟通，不保护纯业务建议。

三秒认题路径：

先看特权 → 再看目的 → 法律建议保 → 业务建议不保 → 选 B

核心法律规则

只记这条就够做题

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的是为了获取或提供法律帮助而作的保密沟通。考场意思：你发给律师的消息，得先看你是不是在问法律意见，而不是在聊生意点子。

保密沟通（confidential communication）要同时满足“为了法律帮助”与“原本想保密”这两个方向。考场意思：只要沟通目的是业务判断、商业前景或一般意见，通常就不进特权。

核心判例： 这是典型的 attorney-client privilege 目的测试：问法律风险的邮件受保护，问经营策略的邮件不受保护。

思维导图

先问：这封邮件是不是在向律师要法律帮助？
是
第一组邮件
问“潜在商标侵权责任”
特权成立：为了法律意见，且原本想保密
结论：可拒绝披露
否
第二组邮件
聊“餐馆生意潜力”
卡死点：这是 business advice，不是 legal advice
结论：不受特权保护
最终答案：只保护第一组，第二组要交。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：两组邮件都能说明被告“明知故犯”，所以都该保密。

但考试真正问的是：它们是不是为了拿到法律帮助；不是为了证明案子里谁更坏。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

第一组邮件是在问 potential trademark infringement liability，属于法律意见；第二组在聊生意前景，落在业务建议，不受特权保护。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权范围误判

✕ A: 把所有律师往来都当特权，忽略第二组在聊 business potential。

❌ 事实误判 | 回信缺失误判

✕ C: 误以为没收到律师回复就不算特权，发问本身也可能受保护。

❌ 法律适用 | 动机混入误判

✕ D: 看到 willfully traded 就想用恶意推翻特权，但特权看沟通目的，不看案情好坏。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定沟通目的，再分法律咨询和商业闲聊，最后只给前者特权。

考场速记

记住一句：问法律就保，谈生意就不保。这题的快筛口令就是先问“legal assistance 还是 business advice”。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
At the start of the trial of a defendant and a codefendant for robbery, the codefendant and her attorney offered to give the prosecutor information about facts that would strengthen the prosecutor's case against the defendant in exchange for leniency toward the codefendant. The prosecutor refused the offer. Shortly thereafter, the codefendant committed suicide.
During the defendant's trial, the prosecutor called the codefendant's attorney and asked him to relate the information that the codefendant had revealed to the attorney.
Is the attorney's testimony admissible?

choices.A: No, because the codefendant's communications are protected by the attorney-client privilege.
choices.B: No, because the plea discussion was initiated by the codefendant rather than by the prosecutor.
choices.C: Yes, because the codefendant intended to disclose the information.
choices.D: Yes, because the information the codefendant gave to her attorney revealing her knowledge of the crime would be a statement against the codefendant's penal interest.

questions.explanation:
Common law privileges protect confidential communications from disclosure, discovery, or admission in federal legal proceedings.† One such privilege applies to attorney-client communications that are

  • made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice and/or representation and
  • intended to be and kept confidential.

As the holder of the attorney-client privilege, the client can refuse to disclose confidential communications to third parties and prevent the attorney from doing so. The privilege remains in effect even after the attorney-client relationship terminates or the client dies (as seen here). However, the client may waive the privilege by:

  • voluntarily disclosing the information to a third party
  • voluntarily giving up the privilege (eg, contractually)
  • failing to timely claim the privilege (eg, after inadvertent disclosure) or
  • failing to object to another's disclosure of confidential information (eg, at trial).

Here, the codefendant shared facts about the robbery with her attorney. That communication was protected by the attorney-client privilege because it was made to obtain legal representation and was, at least initially, intended to be kept confidential. And though the codefendant offered those facts to the prosecutor during a plea discussion, she did not actually disclose them. Her mere offer — regardless of who initiated the discussion — did not waive the privilege, so the attorney's testimony about those facts is inadmissible (Choices B & C).

†Federal courts apply common law privileges except in diversity cases, where state privilege rules apply.

(Choice D) A statement against interest is not barred by the rule against hearsay when the declarant is unavailable (eg, deceased). Here, the deceased codefendant's information was likely against her penal interest because it revealed her knowledge of the crime. But it remains barred by the attorney-client privilege.

📌 Educational Objective

Attorney-client communications are privileged when

  • made to obtain legal advice and/or representation and
  • intended to be and kept confidential.

Merely offering to share the privileged information does not waive the privilege.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (federal common law privileges).
questions.zh-question:
在对一名被告和一名同案被告的抢劫罪审判开始时，该同案被告及其律师向检察官提出，愿意提供有关事实的信息以加强检察官对该被告的指控，以此换取对该同案被告的宽大处理。检察官拒绝了这一提议。此后不久，该同案被告自杀身亡。

在该被告的审判期间，检察官传唤了同案被告的律师，并要求他陈述该同案被告曾向其披露的信息。

该律师的证言是否可被采纳？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为同案被告的沟通内容受律师-当事人特免权的保护。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为认罪协商是由同案被告而非检察官发起的。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为同案被告曾意图披露该信息。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为同案被告提供给其律师的、揭示其对罪行知情的信息，将构成一项对该同案被告刑事利益不利的陈述。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）下，保密沟通（confidential communication）就算后来想拿去谈判，也不会因为“只是提议披露”而自动放弃。

三秒认题路径：

律师沟通 → 想换减刑 → 没真披露 → 特权还在 → 不能说

核心法律规则

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的是为了获取法律建议而作出的、并且本来要保密的沟通，考场意思：只要没放弃，律师和当事人都不能把这段话拿出来。

放弃特权（waiver）通常要靠真正向第三人公开、合同性放弃、迟延主张，或在法庭上不及时反对；考场意思：mere offer 只是“我愿意说”，不是“我已经说了”。

所以这题里，codefendant 只是想用信息去换 leniency，但她并没有实际把保密内容交给检方，特权没有被打破，律师不能代为作证。

核心判例： common law privilege 规则下，仅提议披露（mere offer to disclose） 不等于放弃律师-当事人特权。

思维导图

先看：这段信息是不是 保密沟通（confidential communication）？
是 为了拿法律建议，且本来要保密 → 进入特权保护。
再问：有没有真的 放弃特权（waiver）？
没有 只是和检方谈条件、offer 披露，但没实际公开。
卡死点：mere offer 不是披露，不触发放弃。
结论：律师能不能转述那段话？
不能 特权还在，答案选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她都想把信息拿去换好处了，应该算放弃了。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有把保密内容真正给出去，而不是只在谈判桌上“愿意给”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键事实是 codefendant 只是想用 信息换 leniency，但没有实际披露；保密沟通仍受 律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege） 保护，所以律师不能作证。

❌ 概念混淆 | 起始方误判

✕ B: 把“谁先提议”当成放弃标准，initiated 不是关键。

❌ 事实误判 | 误认已披露

✕ C: 误把“想说”当成“已经说”，intended 不等于放弃。

❌ 法律适用 | 传闻例外错套

✕ D: statement against interest 只管传闻例外，不会打掉特权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判有没有特权，再看有没有真实放弃；只要没实际披露，就别被“愿意交换”带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：想披露（offer to disclose） 不等于 已披露（actual disclosure），特权不会因为嘴上谈条件就消失。

reason.zh: 关于为获得代理而向律师披露事实的证言正是特权保护的核心内容。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A woman entered a guilty plea to a charge of embezzlement. Her attorney hired a retired probation officer as a consultant to gather information for the preparation of a sentencing plan for the woman that would avoid jail. For that purpose, the consultant interviewed the woman for three hours.
Thereafter, the prosecution undertook an investigation of the woman's possible involvement in other acts of embezzlement. The consultant was subpoenaed to testify before a grand jury. The consultant refused to answer any questions concerning his conversation with the woman.
The prosecution has moved for an order requiring the consultant to answer those questions.
How should the court rule on the prosecution's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion in the absence of probable cause to believe the interview developed evidence relevant to the grand jury's inquiry.
choices.B: Deny the motion on the basis of the attorney-client privilege.
choices.C: Grant the motion because exclusionary evidentiary rules do not apply in grand jury proceedings.
choices.D: Grant the motion because the consultant is not an attorney.

questions.explanation:
Common law privileges apply in all stages of a federal legal proceeding, including grand jury proceedings.* This includes the attorney-client privilege, which protects communications—even those made with the attorney's agent—that are (1) made for the purpose of obtaining or providing legal assistance for the client and (2) intended to be and kept confidential.

Here, the attorney hired a consultant to help him prepare the woman's sentencing plan. The consultant therefore acted as the attorney's agent when he interviewed the woman for that purpose. And since that interview was in furtherance of the woman's legal representation and likely intended to be confidential, it is protected by the attorney-client privilege (Choice D). As a result, the prosecution's motion should be denied.

*The Federal Rules of Evidence do not specifically address evidentiary privileges (or constitutional limitations on admissibility). They merely instruct federal courts to apply common law privileges except in diversity cases, where state rules apply.

(Choice A) A grand jury gathers evidence (eg, subpoenas persons to testify) to determine if there is probable cause to indict the accused. But probable cause is not required to subpoena information relevant to the grand jury's investigation. Therefore, this is not a basis for denying the motion.

(Choice C) The Federal Rules of Evidence—except those regarding privilege—do not apply at grand jury proceedings. Therefore, exclusionary evidentiary rules (eg, the rule against hearsay) are inapplicable in a grand jury hearing, but the attorney-client privilege can still be asserted.

📌 Educational Objective

Attorney-client communications are privileged when made to obtain or provide legal assistance for the client and intended to be and kept confidential. This privilege extends to confidential communications between a client and the attorney's agent if those communications are made in furtherance of the legal representation.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 501 (federal common law privileges).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性对一项侵占罪指控承认有罪。她的律师聘请了一名退休的缓刑监督官作为顾问，为该女性准备一份能够避免监禁的量刑计划而收集信息。为此，该顾问与该女性进行了三小时的面谈。

此后，控方对该女性可能涉及的其他侵占行为展开了调查。该顾问被传唤到大陪审团面前作证。该顾问拒绝回答任何关于他与该女性谈话的问题。

控方已提出动议，请求法院下令要求该顾问回答这些问题。

法院应如何裁决控方的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，理由是缺乏合理根据相信该面谈取得了与大陪审团调查相关的证据。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，依据是律师-客户特免权。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为证据排除规则不适用于大陪审团程序。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为该顾问不是律师。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）能不能保护律师代理人为了准备辩护方案而与当事人的保密沟通，所以传唤到大陪审团也不能逼问。

三秒认题路径：

代理人访谈 → 为辩护准备 → 保密沟通 → 特权覆盖 → 拒绝作证

核心法律规则

律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的是为了获取或提供法律帮助而作出的保密沟通，考场意思：只要是为了法律代理，且本来就想保密，就能挡住披露。

这个保护不只罩住律师本人，也罩住律师的代理人（agent），考场意思：律师雇来的顾问如果是在帮忙做法律准备，他问到的保密内容也可能进特权圈。

即使是在大陪审团（grand jury）程序里，特权（privilege）一般也还在，考场意思：不是“进了大陪审团就什么都能问”。

核心判例： Fed. R. Evid. 501 - 联邦法院适用普通法特权；本题里，顾问为准备量刑方案与当事人的保密谈话，属于受保护的律师代理沟通。

思维导图

先问：这是不是“能不能强迫披露”的问题？
YES传唤对象是律师雇来的顾问，且访谈目的是帮忙准备量刑方案。
再问沟通是不是为了法律帮助，而且本来想保密？
卡死点：是。律师代理人做的保密访谈，进 attorney-client privilege。
结论大陪审团可以要证据，但不能把受特权保护的沟通逼出来。
所以法院应当拒绝强制回答，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：大陪审团（grand jury）要查案，应该什么都能问。但考试真正问的是：这段谈话是不是受律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege）保护的保密沟通。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里也一样，不是因为它“看起来相关”就能突破特权。

另一个坑是把“probable cause”误当成传唤门槛；那是大陪审团找线索的标准，不是强迫披露特权沟通的许可。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里顾问是为辩护方案服务的律师代理人，访谈又是为了保密地准备量刑，所以这段沟通落入特权，法院应拒绝强制回答。

❌ 事实误判 | 证据门槛偷换

✕ A: 把probable cause当成传唤门槛了。

❌ 法律适用 | 规则外延误套

✕ C: 把“证据规则不适用”错说成“特权也失效”了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只认律师本人

✕ D: 只看not an attorney，漏掉代理人也受保护。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否为法律帮助而保密沟通”，再看是不是律师代理人，最后排除大陪审团的误导。

考场速记

记住一句：为了法律帮助 + 期待保密 = 特权先挡住；律师雇来的代理人做的保密访谈，也一起算进去。

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question:
A pro se defendant was charged with mail fraud. The defendant pleaded guilty and was sentenced to three years in prison. In response to the sentence, the defendant stated that he had been induced to plead guilty after the prosecutor assured him that the judge would only impose a three-month sentence and a small fine. After hearing evidence on the issue, the judge set aside the judgment and allowed the defendant to withdraw the guilty plea. At trial, the defendant testified to his innocence. The prosecution now seeks to introduce a certified copy of the guilty plea in which the defendant admitted to mail fraud.
Is the certified copy of the guilty plea admissible?

choices.A: No, because the guilty plea was withdrawn.
choices.B: No, because the privilege against self-incrimination bars the admission of a prior incriminating statement.
choices.C: Yes, because a certified guilty plea is a self-authenticating public record.
choices.D: Yes, to impeach the defendant with a prior inconsistent statement.

questions.explanation:
Pleas, plea discussions & related statements
(FRE 410)
General rule The following are not admissible against ∆ in civil or criminal case:
  • Withdrawn guilty pleas
  • Nolo contendere (ie, no contest) pleas
  • Statements made during proceeding on above pleas
  • Statements made during plea discussions with prosecutor
Exceptions
  • Statement during same plea discussions is introduced & both statements should in fairness be considered
  • Criminal proceeding for perjury or false statement if ∆'s statement under oath, on record & with counsel
FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence; ∆ = Defendant.

In civil and criminal cases, statements made during settlement and plea negotiations are generally inadmissible against the defendant who participated in the negotiations or made the plea. This includes guilty pleas that are later withdrawn, since admitting the guilty plea would effectively nullify the order permitting withdrawal. Therefore, the certified copy of the guilty plea at issue here is not admissible against the defendant.

(Choice B) The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination allows a witness (here, the defendant) to refuse to give testimony that tends to incriminate him/herself. But this is not a basis for excluding the certified guilty plea because the privilege, when invoked, only applies to current (not prior) statements.

(Choice C) Tangible evidence (eg, documents) must generally be authenticated through extrinsic evidence that shows the thing is what the proponent claims it to be before it can be admitted. And though certain evidence (eg, certified copies of public records) is self-authenticating and does not require such proof, that evidence can still be excluded on other grounds (as seen here).

(Choice D) The rule excluding statements made during plea negotiations applies even when such statements are offered for impeachment purposes. Therefore, the prosecutor cannot introduce the certified copy of the guilty plea to impeach the defendant's testimony at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

Evidence of statements made during settlement or plea negotiations is generally inadmissible against a defendant. This includes a guilty plea that is later withdrawn.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Evid. 410(a)(1) (evidence of withdrawn guilty plea is inadmissible against defendant).

一名无律师代理的被告被控犯有邮件欺诈罪（mail fraud）。被告作出了有罪答辩，并被判处三年监禁。针对该判决，被告声称，检察官向他保证法官只会判处三个月监禁和一笔小数额的罚款，他因此被诱导作出了有罪答辩。在听取了关于此问题的证据后，法官撤销了该判决，并准许被告撤回其有罪答辩。在庭审中，被告为其无罪作证。控方现试图引入一份经核证的有罪答辩副本，其中被告承认犯有邮件欺诈罪。

这份经核证的有罪答辩副本是否可以采纳为证据？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为该有罪答辩已被撤回。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为反对自证其罪的特权禁止采纳先前的自证其罪陈述。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为经核证的有罪答辩是一份自我认证的公共记录。
zh-choices.D: 可以，用以通过先前的矛盾陈述来弹劾被告。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Privileges and Policy Exclusions - Public policy exclusions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：撤回的有罪答辩（withdrawn guilty plea）能不能被拿来对被告用，答案通常是否定的。

三秒认题路径：

有罪答辩 → 已撤回 → 想拿来反咬 → FRE 410 → 不能用

核心法律规则

联邦证据规则 410（FRE 410）的意思很直白：withdrawn guilty plea，也就是已经撤回的有罪答辩，不能拿来对被告不利使用。plea discussions（答辩协商）里的陈述也一样，考试上就是防止一方先谈判、后被反手当证据打回去。

self-authenticating（自认证）只解决“这份文件是不是它自己说的那份”这个身份问题，不解决“能不能用”这个可采性问题；所以就算是认证过的官方记录，仍然可能被 FRE 410 卡掉。

核心判例： FRE 410(a)(1) 锁定本题结论：撤回的有罪答辩不能作为控方证据对被告使用。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 withdrawn guilty plea？
是进入 FRE 410 的排除规则
想拿来做什么都先别急：impeachment（弹劾）也不行
卡死点：撤回后仍是被规则保护的答辩，不能对被告使用
否再另查别的证据规则
本题结论：控方不能用这份有罪答辩去打被告
答案 A：不可采

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这是一份法院认证过的文件，还是被告自己承认过的内容，所以应该能用。

但考试真正问的是：它是不是 withdrawn guilty plea，只要是，FRE 410 就先把它挡在门外。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

别被“certified copy”带跑：认证解决的是真伪，不是可采性；也别把 self-incrimination 套错到“旧供述能不能进证据”这种题上。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 guilty plea 已被法官撤回，FRE 410 直接禁止控方把它当成不利证据使用，所以不能采。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权对象误判

✕ B: 把 self-incrimination 当成排除旧答辩的理由，方向错了。

❌ 法律适用 | 认证规则错用

✕ C: 盯住 self-authenticating，却忘了认证过也可能被其他规则排除。

❌ 事实误判 | 弹劾场景偷换

✕ D: 想拿撤回答辩去 impeach，但 FRE 410 仍拦着。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“撤回的有罪答辩”这个触发词，再直接套 FRE 410 的排除规则。

考场速记

记住一句话：withdrawn guilty plea 一般不能对被告使用；看到“撤回的答辩”“协商中的陈述”“想拿来弹劾”这三类词，先想 FRE 410。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是上诉例外的记忆法，本题不用，别把它和证据排除混在一起。

reason.zh: 有罪答辩一经撤回，即触发联邦证据规则第410条的排除效力。
